BMW's M4 Convertible Getting a Battery-Electric Neue Klasse Makeover, New Model Spied in a Premiere
20 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
A few hours ago, we wrote about the upcoming BMW M3 Electric , which was just caught in the open flaunting its trippy camouflage and its Neue Klasse design, and now it is time for its open-top sibling to sit under the spotlight.
We are talking about the BMW M4 Convertible’s entirely-new generation, although it is unrelated to the G5X 3 Series, which is based on an updated version of the CLAR platform, as it’s the cabrio version of the latest i3. This means that it packs battery-electric firepower, and it utilizes the same Neue Klasse NAx construction.
Therefore, instead of sharing its nuts and bolts with the upcoming BMW M3, it will have numerous things in common with the first-ever M3 Electric . And this includes the quad-motor setup providing the firepower. We still do not know how much oomph it has, as while some say that it could have either 700 or maybe 800 horsepower, others are convinced that it could boast around 1,000 horsepower.
The latest information coming from the automotive world suggests that an estimated 850 horsepower could be the combined output of the BMW M3 Electric, and if that is indeed the case, then we don’t see why the M4 Convertible Electric won’t have that much oomph available via the right pedal. The output is in metric horsepower, and 850 ps translates to 838 brake horsepower and 625 kilowatts.
Photo: SH Proshots According to the rumor mill, the zero-emission M3 should weight in the region of 2.3 metric tons. That’s over 5,000 pounds. This likely means that all-quiet M4 Convertible will be even heavier. It should share the same battery pack with its four-door sibling, which is understood to have a 100 kWh or so capacity, presumably enabling a WLTP range of around 650 kilometers, or 400+ miles. The battery can be reportedly charged at up to 420 kW, and plugging it in might add up to 350 km (217 miles) of range in approximately ten minutes.
This scooped BMW M4 Convertible Electric is a prototype, albeit an early one, which is why some panels do not properly align. We were tempted to say that it is a mule, but we can clearly see that all body panels are new, and it looks nothing like the current ICE-powered open-top BMW M4. It features the same front fascia as the upcoming M3 Electric, and the front and rear bumpers should also look the same.
These will be inspired by the ones of the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse from earlier this year. Don’t mind the taillights on this scooped tester, because these are provisional. The final ones will likely be identical to those featured on the zero-emission M3. The model sports power-folding rag top that stows away behind a special compartment behind the seats, just like in the current M4 Convertible.
Photo: SH Proshots Some will argue that a folding hardtop would have been better, but a soft top not only helps keep the weight in check (well, as much as it can, because this is still a heavy EV), but also lowers the center of gravity, thus enabling faster cornering credentials. And that’s exactly what it needs if the open-top, zero-emission BMW M4 wants to attract real petrolheads.
While the cabin has yet to open up to the camera, we already know what it will look like. That’s because it is the same Neue Klasse setup as seen on other modern-day Bimmers . Thus, expect the same free-floating infotainment screen, dashboard panel, air vents, and the Panoramic iDrive stretching from one pillar to the other at the bottom of the windscreen. The steering wheel, special trim and upholstery, and other M-infused elements will obviously be shared with the upcoming BMW M3 Electric.
It will be interesting to see how the first-ever battery-electric BMW M4 Convertible feels and drives in the real world, and if it is anything as exciting as the current M4 Competition xDrive Convertible. The latter has 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) to play with from its familiar 3.0-liter TwinPower Turbo straight-six engine, taking 3.6 seconds from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). It is two-tenths of a second slower than the M4 Competition xDrive Coupe for those keeping track of the numbers.
Pricing for the outgoing BMW M4 Competition xDrive Convertible starts at $98,400 in the United States of America, whereas its fixed-roof sibling has an MSRP of $91,500. The lesser M4 Competition Coupe and the base M4 Coupe kick off at $86,400 and $82,200, respectively, and while the former has 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), the latter comes with 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW)., enabling 0-60 mph in 3.8 and 4.1 seconds, respectively.
BMW’s first-ever M3 Electric is understood to launch sometime in 2027, and chances are that the M4 Convertible Electric might follow roughly one year later. The next-gen ICE-powered BMW M3 is also expected to premiere in 2028.
